doc.title: Kristen Korb interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 16, 2000

title: Recognizing individual sounds in older and younger players
summary: Learning to hear voices by listening, Dianne Reeves and Sarah Vaughan, Ray playing Pettiford.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: That was such a big part of that era of the music is people having their own identifiable sound.

And I think today’s guys, I mean everybody’s got their own sound. Even though we’ve got a lot of kind of clone people. But I think if you listen to them long enough I think at this point we’ve listened to those guys so long now that it seems more obvious to us. Where with a lot of these younger guys we still haven’t listened to them enough. Because I’m getting to the point now where I can hear Russell in about three notes. But I’ve been doing a lot of listening. I want to play with him so I’m listening to his music. I’m playing his tunes. And after a while you hear that voice come out in whatever way that that is. But I’ve had friends tease me for a long time because I couldn’t tell saxophone players apart. Man I couldn’t tell a tenor from an alto, I was just pathetic. And then I really started listening to them and playing with the CDs. And all of a sudden it’s just like hearing the voice of a friend. But it’s a matter of that listening. And I think with the younger guys we just haven’t done that enough. But we can certainly hear the influences. You know I listen to Dianne Reeves who is a marvelous singer. I mean her pitch is just pristine, her breath support is just amazing, and she certainly has her own sound. She is

being very eclectic with her music, you know, borrowing from pop, borrowing from jazz. She’s doing a little bit of world music kinds of things. Very creative. But man every once in a while I will hear a Sarah Vaughan lick come out of her, it’s just you know, some of those half step [scats] kinds of things. I just go — that was a Sarah Vaughan thing. But she’s still Dianne. When Ray plays “Swing Until The Girls Come Home,” that’s Oscar Pettiford, but it’s still Ray.
